title: LibGodot Static Library build does not work
body:
### Tested versions

This is a problem in new functionality introduced in 4.6, not a regression; tested in 464ddd4e but I suspect this has been a problem since LibGodot was checked in.

### System information

Manjaro Linux and Windows 10, likely others; GPU irrelevant, compile-time error

### Issue description

The LibGodot static library build doesn't work on Linux or Windows, and likely not on Mac either. The big problem is that the Godot build system builds the final binary by appending libraries to `LIBS`, but building an *actual library* doesn't pull from those (for obvious reasons). I tried coming up with a simple fix and failed miserably, at least on Linux - https://github.com/zorbathut/godot/commit/fd5c741861a7ef82ae6c0b62db98f8ef2225c5e9 is the best I managed. It *works*. But it's not simple. (No guarantees this works anywhere besides Linux GCC.)

I suspect a "real" fix is going to take some build system changes and is outside my area of expertise; I'm also not sure how imporatnt it is for anyone. @kisg, your call on how much time you want to put into this.

Also, just to avoid ambiguity, shared_library works just fine! It's only static_library that is a problem.

It generates a library, but the library is unlinkable due to having *many* missing symbols; obviously a 3MB static library should not pass anyone's sniff test :)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

https://github.com/zorbathut/libgodot_example/tree/static

Run `runit-cpp-static.py`. In theory, it should just work!

(A minimal working LibGodot is kind of chunky, sorry.)
